races.title: County Commission, District 2
races.who: Every Hernando voter (the Aug 18 universal primary was open to all voters)
races.note: Decided in the Aug 18, 2026 universal primary: Kathryn Birren won and the seat is not on the Nov 3 ballot. All five candidates were Republicans with no write-in, so the primary was open to all voters. Appointed incumbent John Mitten did not run.

races.title: County Commission, District 4
races.note: Open seat: Chair Jerry Campbell is not seeking re-election. Jeff Holcomb won the closed Aug 18 Republican primary over Marvin Baynham. On Nov 3 his only opponent is the write-in line; Donald Bigelow is listed by the Supervisor of Elections as a qualified write-in candidate. Write-in names are not printed on the ballot.

races.title: School Board, District 1
races.note: Decided Aug 18, 2026: Dana Pearce won a majority and defeated incumbent Mark C. Johnson. Not on the Nov 3 ballot.

races.title: School Board, District 3
races.note: Decided Aug 18, 2026: incumbent Shannon Rodriguez won a majority. Not on the Nov 3 ballot.

races.title: School Board, District 5
races.note: Runoff: no one won a majority on Aug 18. Kara Champion led incumbent Susan Duval by 7 votes in the official results (3 votes in unofficial results); Amanda Cunningham-Rud was eliminated.

votes.headline: Put a half-cent sales tax for law enforcement on the Nov 3 ballot
votes.inShort: Commissioners passed an ordinance for a half-cent sales tax that would mostly pay for law enforcement equipment and facilities. It only takes effect if voters approve it on Nov 3, 2026.

facts.text: Rate and length: one-half cent, for five years, Jan 1, 2027 through Dec 31, 2031.
Money is split between the county and the City of Brooksville.
Body-worn camera language was removed before it passed.

claims.value: amended to remove body-worn camera language

votes.dateNote: Reported May 5, 2026 (Citizen Portal) and May 8, 2026 (Hernando Sun)
votes.headline: Rejected a second half-cent sales tax vote for roads
votes.inShort: Commissioners voted not to ask voters in November for another half-cent sales tax to fix and maintain roads.

facts.text: Only Champion and Amsler voted yes. The source does not list each no vote by name.

claims.value: only Commissioners Steve Champion and Ryan Amsler voted in favor

facts.text: The exact meeting date of the vote.

votes.headline: Paused new large data centers for one year
votes.inShort: Commissioners approved a one-year moratorium on large-scale data centers while staff study how they affect public facilities and draft any needed planning and zoning changes.

facts.text: The District 2 seat was vacant at the time, so four commissioners voted.

claims.value: seat vacated by Brian Hawkins not yet filled

facts.text: An earlier hearing moved the proposal forward to a second reading.

claims.value: must return for a second reading

facts.text: The county attorney said an outright ban could count as a taking under the Bert Harris Act; a moratorium of a year or less does not.

votes.headline: Rejected a rezoning for duplexes in Hernando Beach
votes.inShort: Commissioners turned down a request to allow 12 units in six duplexes on a Hernando Beach tract. The owner can still build six single-family homes.

facts.text: The Planning and Zoning Commission had recommended denial 3 to 2 on Jul 13.

votes.headline: Approved a rezoning for a concrete batch plant
votes.inShort: Commissioners rezoned agricultural land to a commercial planned development for a concrete batch plant, with conditions including a 30-foot tree buffer.

facts.text: Opponents, including Pasco County residents, raised noise, truck traffic, health, water and environmental concerns.

claims.value: noise, truck traffic, health, water use, environmental
